anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — every ticket row appears verbatim in `## Acceptance criteria`, and each has a disposition that matches the human answer. The 60s row is deferred to a tracker ref, which the human chose (C). The export does not need the 60s timing row to work, so the deferral passes the operates-without-it test. The mailer row is correctly routed to acme/mailer.

findings:
- [major] gap @ Design: "the mailer handoff reuses the existing export-ready event" — The spec does not say whether widgets publishes this event, when it does so (on every GET to /widgets/export.csv?), or what payload it carries. In particular, it does not say which download link goes in the event, given the export is a synchronous download with no stored artifact. Mailer's row depends on this contract, and no test covers the widgets side of it. → Either state "widgets emits `<event name>` with `{user_id, download_url: /widgets/export.csv}` when <trigger>" and add a request test asserting the emission, or state explicitly that widgets emits nothing new and name the existing producer. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Design: "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000" — The human deferral reason says "paging ships next sprint" (acme/widgets#78), but this change already batches its reads. An implementer cannot tell whether this batching is the #78 paging work being pulled forward or a separate internal read strategy. → Say that batching is an internal read strategy only, distinct from the #78 paging, or drop it. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Design: "The benchmark uses 10000 local widgets…" / Verification: "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope" — The row is deferred, so the "when in-scope" condition is never true here. That leaves it unclear whether the benchmark is built in this change. → State "benchmark not built or run in this change; tracked in acme/widgets#78" or move the benchmark text into a deferred note. — probed: none
- [minor] external-ref @ Acceptance criteria: "deferred: acme/widgets#78" — The human answer gave a reason ("paging ships next sprint"), but the AC row drops it, so a reader must open #78 to learn why. → Write the row as "deferred: acme/widgets#78 - paging ships next sprint". — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Design: "Encode id, name, and status with standard CSV quoting" — The spec does not name the quoting standard (RFC 4180?) or the line ending. It also does not define the status value written (raw enum vs. display label), and it does not say whether leading `=+-@` in name is neutralized to prevent CSV formula injection. → Name RFC 4180 with CRLF, define the status representation, and decide on formula-prefix handling with a test case. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes — The design covers the three in-scope widgets criteria, preserves the explicitly approved performance deferral, and leaves email delivery with mailer.
findings:
- [major] external-ref @ Design: “the mailer handoff reuses the existing export-ready event” — The handoff depends on an event contract that is neither named nor inlined. The spec does not say when the synchronous export emits it or how its payload supplies the download link mailer needs → Inline the relevant event contract, including emission timing and the download-link payload, and specify a widgets-side test for that handoff without taking on mailer delivery. — probed: none
